content.content:
# Resend — transactional email for Next.js Resend sends an app's transactional email (welcome emails, password resets, receipts) through a small HTTP API with delivery logs, webhooks and domain verification. The official Node.js library `resend` wraps the whole Resend REST API, has typed responses and works in Node.js 18+, serverless and edge runtimes. ## Install ```bash npm install resend ``` ## 1. Environment variables `.env.local`: ``` RESEND_API_KEY=re_placeholder RESEND_FROM_EMAIL=hello@example.com ``` The API key is created in the Resend dashboard (API Keys). The From address must be on a domain you have verified in Resend, or `onboarding@resend.dev` while testing. ## 2. Create a client `src/lib/resend.ts`: ```ts import { Resend } from "resend"; export const resend = new Resend(process.env.RESEND_API_KEY!); ``` Use the client only in server code (route handlers, server actions, server components). Never expose the API key to the browser. ## 3. Send an email ```ts import { resend } from "@/lib/resend"; const { data, error } = await resend.emails.send({ from: process.env.RESEND_FROM_EMAIL!, to: "user@example.com", subject: "Welcome!", html: "

Thanks for signing up.

", text: "Thanks for signing up.", }); ``` `data.id` is the message id; use it to look the email up in the dashboard logs. ## 4. Send with a React template Write the email as a React component and pass it with `react`; Resend renders it to HTML: ```tsx import { resend } from "@/lib/resend"; import { PasswordResetEmail } from "@/emails/password-reset"; await resend.emails.send({ from: process.env.RESEND_FROM_EMAIL!, to: "user@example.com", subject: "Reset your password", react: PasswordResetEmail({ name: "Ada", actionUrl: "https://example.com/reset?token=..." }), }); ``` The `@react-email/components` package gives layout primitives for email clients; plain JSX works too. ## 5. Handle errors `emails.send` does not throw on a refused message: it resolves to `{ data: null, error }` with the error `name` and `message` from Resend (invalid API key, unverified domain, rate limit). Check `error` where the email is triggered so a failed email does not break the request that caused it. ## Why teams pick Resend - Built for developers: one API call to send, typed SDK, React templates in the codebase. - Delivery logs, bounces and webhooks live in the same dashboard as the API keys. - Domain verification with DKIM and SPF guided from the dashboard. ------ # Postmark — transactional email for Next.js Postmark sends an app's transactional email (welcome emails, password resets, receipts) with high delivery rates, bounce and spam processing, and detailed statistics. The official Node.js library `postmark` covers the whole Postmark REST API, uses the native Fetch API and has no runtime dependencies (Node 18+). ## Install ```bash npm install postmark ``` ## 1. Environment variables `.env.local`: ``` POSTMARK_SERVER_TOKEN=server_token_placeholder POSTMARK_FROM_EMAIL=hello@example.com ``` The server token belongs to one Postmark server (Servers → API Tokens). The From address must be a confirmed sender signature or sit on a verified domain. ## 2. Create a client `src/lib/postmark.ts`: ```ts import { ServerClient } from "postmark"; export const postmark = new ServerClient(process.env.POSTMARK_SERVER_TOKEN!); ``` Use the client only in server code (route handlers, server actions, server components). Never expose the server token to the browser. ## 3. Send an email ```ts import { postmark } from "@/lib/postmark"; await postmark.sendEmail({ From: process.env.POSTMARK_FROM_EMAIL!, To: "user@example.com", Subject: "Welcome!", HtmlBody: "

Thanks for signing up.

", TextBody: "Thanks for signing up.", MessageStream: "outbound", }); ``` `outbound` is the default transactional message stream. Keep transactional and broadcast email in separate streams. ## 4. Send with a template Create the template once in the Postmark dashboard, then send it by alias: ```ts await postmark.sendEmailWithTemplate({ From: process.env.POSTMARK_FROM_EMAIL!, To: "user@example.com", TemplateAlias: "password-reset", TemplateModel: { name: "Ada", action_url: "https://example.com/reset?token=..." }, MessageStream: "outbound", }); ``` `TemplateId` (a number) works in place of `TemplateAlias`. ## 5. Handle errors `sendEmail` returns a promise that rejects with a typed error from `postmark`'s `Errors` export when Postmark refuses the message (inactive recipient, unconfirmed sender, invalid token). Catch it where the email is triggered so a failed email does not break the request that caused it. ## Why teams pick Postmark - Built for transactional email: high delivery rates, with bounce and spam handling included. - Templates live in the dashboard, so copy changes do not need a deploy. - Detailed delivery statistics and inbound email parsing come with the same account. # Notely A small team notes app. Next.js App Router + TypeScript + Tailwind. ## Status - Users live in `src/lib/users.ts` as an in-memory list. - `/dashboard` shows the current user and the team. - There is no sign-in, no billing, and no email yet. ## Develop ```bash npm run dev ``` dashboard favicon.ico globals.css layout.tsx page.tsx src/app/dashboard: page.tsx

content.text:
Welcome and password-reset emails are now sent through Resend, wired into `src/lib/users.ts`. I haven't sent a real email, since there's no API key here. Lint passes.

`tsc` reports one error, `Cannot find name 'LayoutProps'` in `src/app/layout.tsx`. It also appears with my changes stashed, so it was already there. Next generates that type at build time.

**Why Resend:** it's a single small dependency with an API that returns errors instead of throwing. It also needs no dashboard-managed templates, so the email copy stays in the repo.

**What changed**
- **`src/lib/email.ts` (new):** `sendWelcomeEmail` and `sendPasswordResetEmail`, each sending HTML and plain text with user input escaped. A failed send is logged and returns `false` rather than throwing, so a mail problem never breaks the request that triggered it.
- **`src/lib/users.ts`:**
  - **`createUser`:** this didn't exist, so I added it. It normalizes the email, rejects duplicates, adds the user and sends the welcome email.
  - **`requestPasswordReset`:** also new. It creates a random token valid for 1 hour and emails a `/reset-password?token=…` link. It does nothing visible for unknown emails, so it can't be used to check which accounts exist.
  - **`consumePasswordResetToken`:** also new. A token works once and is stored only as a hash.
- **`.env.example`:** `RESEND_API_KEY`, `RESEND_FROM_EMAIL` and `APP_URL`, all placeholders. `.gitignore` ignored every `.env*` file, so I added an exception for `.env.example`. The README status line is updated.

**Not built:**
- **Reset page and passwords:** there is no `/reset-password` page, because the app has no passwords or sign-in yet. The reset link points at a page that doesn't exist until you build it. `consumePasswordResetToken` is ready for that page to call.
- **Callers:** nothing calls `createUser` or `requestPasswordReset` yet, since there is no signup or forgot-password route.
- **Storage:** users and reset tokens are in memory, like the existing user list, so they reset on restart.

Before real use, set `RESEND_FROM_EMAIL` to an address on a domain you've verified in Resend. If `RESEND_FROM_EMAIL` is unset, the sender falls back to `onboarding@resend.dev`, which only works for testing.
